## 26f313fdf812

**Classification: No issue found within the documented generator domain; one
out-of-domain scope question retained.** I did not modify this audit target.
The audited generator SHA-256 is
`7860fb33fe86183a8f0898e568c0efdf569cbcdea4ca5dafd455699001429d4e`;
the executed/catalog Racket rule hash is `80930b679862`.

I checked the generator's object extraction, top-left ordering, cell-area
comparison, tie/rank curriculum, override observability, semantic rivals, and
sample diversity. The focused `lint`, `selfcheck`, `semantic_gate`, `override`,
and `diversity` stages all passed; their source-bound reports are under
`checks/audit/26f313fdf812-*`.

A plausible rule outside the declared domain is **group all pixels of one color
as one object**, rather than treating disconnected same-color components as
separate objects. It fits all canonical examples and all normal generator draws
because the generator explicitly requires every nonzero color to form exactly
one connected object. I retained an exact disagreement input in
`checks/audit/26f313fdf812-domain-question/input.json`: it has two disconnected
color-2 objects of areas 2 and 3 plus one color-4 object of area 4. Canonical
Racket returns the 3×3 component comparison matrix
`[[1,3,3],[2,1,3],[2,2,1]]`; the color-grouping rival returns the 2×2 matrix
`[[1,2],[3,1]]`. The supported `arcpuzzles apply` receipt is
`checks/audit/26f313fdf812-domain-question/racket.json`, and the rival is
`rival.json`.

This is **not a reproduced generator defect**: `self_check` rejects the witness
with `each nonzero color must form one connected object; split colors: [2]`, so
it does not belong to the documented generator domain. It is a domain question
for maintainers only: if the intended training domain should include repeated
colors across disconnected objects, the generator should add such cases;
otherwise the current invariant is explicit and the checked in-domain behavior
is clean.
